items.title: Remote-approval flow for headless confirm_blocking() + dashboard LLM backend status
items.notes: core/pending_approvals.py (thread-safe ApprovalStore, event-based blocking, fails closed on timeout) + core/notify.py (ntfy push -- new integration, no ntfy setup existed in this codebase before; ntfy_base_url/ntfy_topic added as new config keys). confirm_blocking() registers a pending approval, fires the push, and blocks until dashboard/server.py's new POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve|deny resolves it or times out. Dashboard also gained GET /api/llm-status surfacing core.llm_client.get_llm_backend_status() (active backend + real IP/host, including the fallback IP), polled in app.html. Verified via 9 tests + full suite; caught and fixed an old test that started blocking for the real 120s default timeout once confirm_blocking() became a genuine blocking call.

items.title: Pending approvals don't survive a restart
items.notes: Decision: approvals stay in-memory by design. An approval belongs to the thread blocked on it; restoring one after a restart could approve an action nobody is waiting on, and timeout-deny is the safe default. The real gap was that a restart made the request vanish without a trace, so confirm_blocking now writes an audit entry (tool=approval, action=requested, decision=pending, with the approval id and message) the moment a request is created; a pending row with no later approved/denied row in /audit means it was interrupted. Added 'pending' to the /audit decision filter. Not implemented: surfacing interrupted requests proactively on the next startup.

items.title: ntfy push for approvals is one-shot, no retry/queue
items.notes: core/notify.keep_notifying runs on a daemon thread started by HeadlessUI.confirm_blocking: a failed first push is retried after 5s/15s/45s, and one 'Still waiting' reminder goes out if the approval is unanswered ntfy_remind_after_s (default 60, 0 disables) after the first push. Stops the instant the approval resolves or its deadline passes (the approval's event is set when confirm_blocking returns, including on timeout); never delays the wait. First push stays synchronous so the exactly-one-push-per-request test still holds. Mocked-network tests only; no real ntfy server was contacted.

items.title: [F1] Prompt and tool-schema tuning per model, driven by benchmark results
items.notes: Completed Qwen 2.5 1.5B prompt/schema tuning with repeat isolated full-suite evidence and a safe model tool-call benchmark. Two profile-enabled runs scored 102/107 both times (95%); the matched no-guidance controls scored 94/107 and 89/107 (88% and 83%), an average gain of 10.5 cases / 9.8 percentage points. Personal-fact honesty rose from 1/8 in both controls to 7/8 and 8/8 with the profile. Average p50 was 3.10s with profile vs 2.97s without (+131ms); p95 varied and remains host-sensitive. Improvements are concentrated in honesty, with some per-case variation in reasoning/instruction; reversal and translation are not consistently solved. The actual tool-call suite scored 8/8; no schema change was warranted. JSON-only output now passes after fixing bare JSON misclassification in tool-call recovery. Evaluation CLI supports --disable-model-guidance for repeatable control runs and isolates chat history. Remaining weak cases are model capability limits, not evidence for further prompt/schema edits in this item.

items.title: Small-model replies that promise but never act ('I will research...') - retry once forcing the tool call
items.notes: Done: core/conversation_core.py now detects a short first-person promise reply ('I'll research that now') with no tool call and retries the round ONCE with a nudge (llm.promise_without_action_retry metric). Conservative detector: <=400 chars, no '?' or code fence, first/last sentence must open with a promise + action verb. Only when tools were offered and the reply wasn't truncated. Promise + nudge stay in the turn's working messages, never in saved chat history. 33 tests in tests/test_promise_without_action.py incl. 4 that drive the real loop with a scripted LLM. items.title: Push-to-talk / wake-word default so background media is never transcribed
items.notes: Done: new core/listen_mode.py + wiring in core/listen_loops.py. listen_mode = auto (default) | always | wake | ptt. auto = wake word if ready, else push-to-talk (global hotkey ctrl+alt+space, config ptt_shortcut), else always-listening with a WRN. PTT opens the mic for one utterance, closes after ptt_idle_secs (6) without speech, never closes mid-sentence (VAD.in_speech). Any fallback (no keyboard pkg, hotkey registration fails) lands on always-listening with a warning, never deaf. Explicit legacy wake_word_enabled is honoured when listen_mode is unset, so existing setups are unchanged. 24 tests in tests/test_listen_mode.py incl. end-to-end runs of the real mic loop (background audio never transcribed in ptt; control proves it is transcribed in always). tests/test_mark_lv_ports.py made hermetic. Config key is ptt_shortcut, not ptt_hotkey: tests/test_invariants.py flags any config key containing 'key' as a possible secret. BEHAVIOR CHANGE: a config with neither listen_mode nor wake_word_enabled now resolves to auto, i.e. push-to-talk on machines with the keyboard package -- set listen_mode=always to restore the old always-open mic. Not tried with a real mic/hotkey on Windows yet.
